summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder and recent bereavement was admitted at 35 weeks for recurrent severe depression and akathisia, requiring continuation of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) during pregnancy. She was found to have new-onset hypothyroidism, which was treated with levothyroxine. After several ECT sessions with good psychiatric response, she developed gestational hypertension and signs of preeclampsia, prompting induction of labor. She delivered a healthy infant via spontaneous vaginal delivery after a prolonged induction, with manual extraction of a retained placenta. Her postpartum course was uncomplicated, with resolution of psychiatric symptoms and stable vital signs. She was discharged home on quetiapine, levothyroxine, and prenatal vitamins, with plans for ongoing outpatient ECT and psychiatric follow-up.
problems: Gestational [pregnancy-induced] hypertension without significant proteinuria, third trimester
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases complicating pregnancy, third trimester
